'''Josh Aaron Cassada''' (born July 18, 1973) is an American physicist, test pilot, and former [[NASA]] astronaut. Prior to his selection to join NASA in 2013, Cassada served as a test pilot in the [[US Navy]], and has over 3,500 hours in more than 40 aircraft, and 23 combat missions.  In August 2018, Cassada was selected for [[CTS-1]], the first operational mission of the [[Boeing CST-100 Starliner]],<ref name="nasabio">{{cite web |last=Whiting |first=Melanie |date=August 4, 2018 |title=Josh Cassada |url=https://www.nasa.gov/astronauts/biographies/josh-a-cassada/biography |access-date=October 24, 2018 |publisher=[[NASA]]}}</ref><ref name="training_complete">{{cite web |last=Dunbar |first=Brian |date=August 7, 2017 |title=NASA's Newest Astronauts Complete Training |url=https://www.nasa.gov/feature/nasa-s-newest-astronauts-complete-training |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220627134619/https://www.nasa.gov/feature/nasa-s-newest-astronauts-complete-training/ |archive-date=June 27, 2022 |access-date=September 28, 2018 |publisher=[[NASA]]}}</ref><ref name="nasacc_crew">{{cite web |last=Potter |first=Sean |date=August 3, 2018 |title=NASA Assigns Crews to First Test Flights, Missions on Commercial Spacecraft |url=https://www.nasa.gov/press-release/nasa-assigns-crews-to-first-test-flights-missions-on-commercial-spacecraft |access-date=September 28, 2018 |website=NASA}}</ref> but subsequently reassigned to [[SpaceX Crew-5]].

==Early life and education==
Josh Aaron Cassada  was born on July 18, 1973, in [[San Diego, California]], and raised in [[White Bear Lake, Minnesota]].<ref name="spacefactsbio">{{cite web |date=April 18, 2018 |title=Josh Aaron Cassada |url=http://www.spacefacts.de/bios/astronauts/english/cassada_josh.htm |access-date=October 24, 2018 |work=Biographies of U.S. Astronauts |publisher=Spacefacts}}</ref> Cassada graduated from [[Albion College]] in 1995 with a Bachelor of Arts in physics. He was a member of Sigma Chi Alpha Pi Chapter Fraternity at [[Albion College]]. He attended the [[University of Rochester]] for graduate school and received a Master of Arts and a doctorate in physics in 1997 and 2000, respectively.  While at the University of Rochester, Cassada studied high-energy particle physics and conducted research at the [[Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory]].<ref name=nasabio />

==Military career==
After completing his graduate work, Cassada commissioned as a naval officer in 2000.  He completed flight training in 2001, and became a [[P-3 Orion]] pilot in [[VP-8]] at [[NAS Brunswick]] in 2002.  Cassada deployed in support of [[Operation Iraqi Freedom]] and [[Operation Enduring Freedom]], and flew in the humanitarian [[Operation Unified Assistance]] after the [[2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami|2004 Indian Ocean tsunami]]. In 2006, he graduated from the [[U.S. Naval Test Pilot School]], and served as a P-3 Orion and [[P-8 Poseidon]] test pilot at [[NAS Patuxent River]].  Cassada served as the P-8A Airworthiness Project Officer, and was a [[T-38 Talon]] and [[Beechcraft T-6 Texan II|T-6 Texan]] instructor test pilot. In 2011, he worked for the [[Defense Contract Management Agency]] at [[Boeing]] in [[Seattle, Washington]], where he oversaw operations and contracts for the P-8 Poseidon, [[KC-46 Pegasus]], [[E-3 Sentry]], and the [[US Marine Corps]] [[UAV]] programs.<ref name=nasabio />  Outside of the military, he founded Quantum Opus, a superconducting instrument manufacturer, with two of his classmates from Albion College.<ref name="quantumopus">{{cite web |date=2018 |title=About Us |url=https://www.quantumopus.com/web/about-us/ |access-date=October 24, 2018 |publisher=Quantum Opus}}</ref>

==NASA career==
In 2013, Cassada was selected for [[NASA Astronaut Group 21]], and completed training in July 2015.  He has served as [[Flight controller#Spacecraft communicator (CAPCOM)|CAPCOM]] in support of [[International Space Station]] operations, and worked on the development of the [[Orion (spacecraft)|Orion]] and [[Commercial Crew Development|Commercial Crew]] programs.  In August 2018, he and [[Sunita Williams]] were selected to fly on [[CTS-1]], the first operational flight of [[Boeing]]'s [[CST-100 Starliner]] spacecraft.<ref name=nasabio /><ref name=nasacc_crew /> However, due to delays in Starliner's development, Cassada was reassigned to SpaceX's Crew-5 flight.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Kurkowski |first1=Seth |date=2021-10-06 |title=NASA reassigns Starliner crew members to SpaceX Crew-5 mission |url=https://spaceexplored.com/2021/10/06/nasa-reassigns-starliner-crew-members-to-spacex-crew-5-mission/ |access-date=2021-10-06 |website=Space Explored |language=en-US}}</ref> Cassada retired from NASA on October 1, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-01 |title=Three-time Spacewalker Josh Cassada to Retire from NASA |url=https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/three-time-spacewalker-josh-cassada-to-retire-from-nasa/#:~:text=NASA%20astronaut%20Josh%20Cassada%20retired%20Oct.%201,%20after,aviator%20with%20more%20than%20two%20decades%20of%20service |access-date=2024-10-01 |website=Space Explored |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Cassada and his wife, Megan, have two children.<ref name=nasabio />

==Awards and honors==
Cassada graduated [[summa cum laude]] from Albion College, and received a teaching award from the University of Rochester's physics and astronomy department.  In his military career, Cassada was awarded the [[Defense Meritorious Service Medal]], three Navy and Marine Corps Commendation Medals, including the [[Combat V]] device, and the [[Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medal]].<ref name=nasabio />
